messages:
rachel (product): Leaving a short follow-up thread for the pricing/usage q&a from today. Please post brief clarifying Qs.
priya (support): Are embedding units billed differently than text gen tokens? Customers keep asking.
sam (finance): Yes, embeddings use an "embedding unit" metric (per-1024-dim chunk) and are billed separately from text gen tokens. Pricing docs have the exact mapping.
liam (eng): On rate-limit granularity: we support both RPS and tokens-per-second for model endpoints. RPS protects request rate, TPS protects cost/throughput.
priya (support): If a customer sets both, which wins? They're confused about double limits.
liam (eng): The strictest applicable limiter wins. We enforce: per-route RPS -> per-account TPS -> project-level budget. That prevents accidental cost overruns.
diana (cofounder): Quick note on "slo credits": if we fail an SLA, we issue SLO credits as a percentage of monthly fees, separate from usage credits.
sam (finance): Correct. SLO credits do not increase a customer's usable credit pool; they reduce invoice amounts on the next billing cycle.
priya (support): A customer hit a "safety hold" during a POC because of anomalous traffic. What is the user-visible message?
ops-bot: safety-hold: Applied to org "orchard-labs". Reason: anomalous spike detected. Contact support to lift.
liam (eng): Safety holds are different from quota limits: they block particle endpoints until ops reviews. We surface a diagnostic URL in the account banner.
rachel (product): Do we auto-notify admins before a safety hold? Customers want preemptive alerts.
ops-bot: Scheduled alert rule: pre-hold warning at 3x baseline traffic and critical at 10x. Admin email + in-console banner.
sam (finance): About trial credits: we support org-level trial pools and per-project allocations. By default trials are org-pooled unless a sales rep requested siloing.
priya (support): For private/on-prem evals, can we apply hosted trial credits? Customer wanted to run mixed managed/self-managed infra.
liam (eng): Hosted credits only apply when requests route through Redwood-managed control plane. If the private deployment sends metering back to our billing endpoint (contracted), we can consume credits. Otherwise self-hosted=no hosted credits.
diana (cofounder): Refund/credit policy recap: one-off user errors often get a goodwill credit; systemic platform issues get SLO credits per contract.
sam (finance): Refund requests: please collect request id, org id, time range, and any job ids. We try to respond within 3 business days.
priya (support): Any guidance on SDK retry logic for mixed limits (RPS + TPS)? Customers want a simple pattern to implement.
liam (eng): Recommended: check `X-RateLimit-Remaining` and `X-RateLimit-Reset` per response; if 429 use `Retry-After`. For token throttles, SDKs should throttle generation speed (token pacing) rather than full request backoff.
rachel (product): New product ask: should we advertise burst as "seconds of extra TPS" or as "burst credits"? Thoughts?
diana (cofounder): Keep it tangible. Use "burst credits" (X tokens/minute for Y minutes) plus a simple cost calculator in console.
sam (finance): We'll publish a sample cost table and a contract checklist for enterprise reps.
priya (support): Last: if a customer accidentally leaves a synthetic load test running, and burns credits, can we offer a one-time exception?
diana (cofounder): One-time exceptions are fine for genuine mistakes; escalate to finance for >$5k credits.
sam (finance): Yep. We prefer issuing credits to refunds on invoices in most cases.
ops-bot: follow-up-ticket created: #AH-4721 (pricing/usage clarifications).
rachel (product): Thanks all 12 we'll consolidate answers into the FAQ and ping the thread when it's live.
